entry.title: Invited speaker: Michael Wilson from the University of Toronto, Canada

link.title: Invited speaker: Michael Wilson from the University of Toronto, Canada

entry.content:
Michael is a fascinating scientist working at the interface of comparative genomics🧬, bioinformatics🖥️, and molecular biology🥼. His research uses cross-species approaches to uncover fundamental principles of genome regulation and understand how these mechanisms shape development and human disease.

Title of the seminar: Using comparative and functional genomics to understand cardiovascular development and disease gene regulation.

If you want to know more about his 👩‍🔬 group 🧑‍🔬 you can check their website!! (Wilson Lab)

entry.title: Scientific Retreat in Baeza
entry.content:
We recently gathered in Baeza for our scientific retreat along with Lupiañez Lab and Acemel Lab, hosted at the beautiful Sede Antonio Machado (UNIA). Over several days, we shared updates on our ongoing projects, discussed recent findings, and explored new ideas that will help shape our future experiments and research directions.

Great science starts with great conversations, and this retreat was full of them. Thanks to everyone for the engaging discussions and inspiring atmosphere!

entry.title: Invited speaker: Margarida Cardoso from the Francis Crick Institute

link.title: Invited speaker: Margarida Cardoso from the Francis Crick Institute

entry.content:
Margarida is a highly enthusiastic scientist conducting outstanding research on how new organs originate and how they evolve in form and function across species, using the placenta in fishes 🐟 as one of her main model systems. Her lab investigates the genetic, cellular, and developmental mechanisms underlying the repeated and independent evolution of placentas in mammals 🐁 and fishes 🐟. Don’t miss the opportunity to discover her exciting science and meet her in person!

Title of the seminar: The evolution of new cell types and organs.

If you want to know more about her 👩‍🔬 group 🧑‍🔬 you can check their website!! (Cardoso Moreira lab)

entry.title: Fany as an invited speaker in the conference L’évolution des mécanismes du développement organized by Denis Duboule

link.title: Fany as an invited speaker in the conference L’évolution des mécanismes du développement organized by Denis Duboule

entry.content:
Fany was invited to present at the conference “L’évolution des mécanismes du développement”, organized by Denis Duboule.

The symposium focused on how developmental processes create biological variation, the basis of evolution. While natural selection determines which traits persist, the meeting addressed a more fundamental question: how new forms arise in the first place.
entry.summary: Fany was invited to present at the conference “L’évolution des mécanismes du développement”, organized by Denis Duboule.

entry.title: Welcome to the lab, Fabian!🎉🎉
entry.content:
We’re thrilled to welcome Fabian Lim to the Real Lab as a postdoctoral researcher.

At the Real Lab, Fabian will be exploring the fascinating biology of the Iberian mole, comparing the 3D genomic architecture and enhancers between moles and mice to uncover mechanisms of evolutionary adaptation behind specialized traits.

entry.title: Limb development and regeneration: quantitative, ecological, and diversification studies. March 2026, Tokyo (Japan) 🇯🇵🧬

link.title: Limb development and regeneration: quantitative, ecological, and diversification studies. March 2026, Tokyo (Japan) 🇯🇵🧬

entry.content:
Fany was an invited speaker at the congress Limb Development and Regeneration: Quantitative, Ecological, and Diversification Studies, held in Japan.

This EMBO Workshop focused on understanding how genetic programs, cellular dynamics, and environmental factors shape limb development, regeneration, and morphological diversification across species. By integrating quantitative approaches, evolutionary perspectives, and ecological insights, the meeting fostered cross‑disciplinary dialogue to advance our understanding of limb biology.

During the congress, Fany had the pleasure of delivering her first lecture as an EMBO Young Investigator Programme (EMBO‑YIP) member.
entry.summary: Fany was an invited speaker at the congress Limb Development and Regeneration: Quantitative, Ecological, and Diversification Studies, held in Japan.

entry.title: Symposium of Early Career Research Investigators of Seville in Biomedicine & Biology (SECRIS) 2026

link.title: Symposium of Early Career Research Investigators of Seville in Biomedicine & Biology (SECRIS) 2026

entry.content:
SECRIS (Seville Early Career Research Investigators Symposium) is an initiative created to provide a shared meeting space for early‑career researchers from the three main biomedical research centres in Seville: IBiS, CABIMER, and CABD. Coordinated by Prof. Gabriel Núñez (University of Michigan / Visiting Professor at IBiS) and organised by predoctoral researchers from the three centres, the symposium aims to showcase early‑career research, promote interaction, and foster new scientific collaborations across institutions in the city.

Building on the success of its first edition, the goal of SECRIS 2026 is to further strengthen inter‑institutional connections among early‑career scientists in Seville, encourage interdisciplinary dialogue, and consolidate a sustainable local network that supports collaboration, visibility, and career development for emerging researchers.

Keren and Miguel (Lupiáñez Lab), and Nacho and Rubén (Real Lab), actively participated as members and organisers within the SECRIS committee, contributing to the coordination and development of the symposium and reinforcing the collaborative spirit of the initiative.
